title: Adaptive windowed prefill-decode arbitration with age-based fairness
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Mixed workloads (short-chat, long-completion, high-batch embeddings) suffer either from head-of-line latency when we favor throughput or from throughput collapse when we prioritize strict single-request latency. Current phase-splitting schedulers treat prefill and decode almost as independent lanes and rely on static quotas which underutilize KV cache locality and hardware fast-paths. Goal: implement an adaptive windowed arbitration that dynamically splits prefill vs decode work into small time windows, uses request age and token phase to drive admission, and preserves KV cache locality while providing bounded p95 latency for latency-sensitive traffic.
decisions: Use a sliding time-window allocator (default 20ms) that groups prefill and decode tokens for arbitration to improve batching without starving short requests.
Introduce an age score per request (ms since arrival) that increases admission priority linearly after a threshold; prevents starvation of long-running prefill-heavy requests.
Prefer keeping prefill fragments co-located to leverage KV cache hits; avoid splitting prefill fragments across GPUs unless necessary.
Expose two knobs to users: latency_tier (low/medium/high) and fairness_mode (strict/soft); defaults preserve existing SLOs for P0 customers.
Kernel selection changes: route latency-tier requests to kernels with lower per-token latency (fp16 fused attention if available) and lower batch sizes to keep tail latency tight.
Fallback: if windowed allocator cannot meet p95 SLO within capacity, automatic degrade to single-request hedged policy for latency-tier traffic.
tradeoffs: Smaller windows reduce p95 but increase per-token CPU/GPU overhead and reduce batching efficiency (token throughput drop ~5-12% in early experiments).
Age-based priority reduces starvation but may slightly increase average latency for new low-priority requests; tunable by slope parameter.
Co-locating prefill fragments improves KV cache hit-rate but complicates autoscaler packing decisions; requires estimator to predict co-location benefit.
Routing latency-tier traffic to low-latency kernels reduces throughput on those accelerators and can increase cost; mitigated by routing by region and time-of-day.
Complexity: implementing windowed arbitration and age-scores requires changes to token allocator, metrics, and observability; rollout will be gradual behind a feature flag.
tasks: Spec: write concise design doc and microflow diagrams (Confluence) - Aisha
Simulator: extend the existing load simulator to model mixed mixes with TTL and age scoring - Marco
Scheduler: implement windowed allocator prototype in runtime scheduler (feature flagged) - eng-scheduler team
Kernel routing: add latency-tier kernel selection logic (hook into kernel catalog) - infra-kernels
Tests: create unit tests, integration tests, and a soak job in staging with 24h mixed-workload replay
Benchmark: run 3 config sweeps (window=10/20/40ms; age-slope=0.0/0.5/1.0) and collect p50/p95/p99 latency and tokens/sec
Dashboard: add Grafana panels (p95 by latency_tier, Jain's fairness index, KV cache hit-rate) - telemetry
Docs: API spec for latency_tier and fairness_mode, examples for customers - docs
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for latency_tier=low must be <= 120ms on the standard chat benchmark at target load
Throughput degradation for mixed workload (baseline: current static allocator) must be <= 10% for default config
Fairness: Jain's index for request-level token allocation across tenants >= 0.92 on benchmark runs
KV cache hit-rate must not drop by more than 5% from baseline when co-location heuristics enabled
Feature gated rollouts: the scheduler must be toggleable per-cluster and support A/B canary with traffic split
Automated tests and staging soak passing for 24h before production rollout
